comparison: Both evaluate the TARDIS methodology and conceptual framework as SUPPORTED (C7-C9, C34-C41, C142, C165-C166). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the two-step process and 1000-fold throughput claim. Peer reviewers affirm novelty and effectiveness with all three reviewers confirming solid data, though peer review also includes novelty claims C171-C172 not in OpenEval R1.

Both evaluate barcode library generation and diversity as SUPPORTED (C48, C62-C67, C75-C79, C84-C85). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of complexing PCR, diversity metrics, and theoretical maximum calculations. Peer review confirms conclusions are supported by data and notes important controls. Peer review includes C10 not present in OpenEval R2.

Both address jackpotting and array formation phenomena as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R3 focuses on jackpotting frequency analysis (C70-C73, C86-C87, C90-C92) with mechanistic speculation appropriately acknowledged. Peer R6 covers broader array formation observations (C70-C74, C86-C92, C190-C196) including mechanistic explanations, treating these as important observations and considerations.

Both evaluate the correlation between array and integration frequencies as SUPPORTED (C49, C97-C101). OpenEval emphasizes statistical robustness with high correlation coefficients and identification of outliers. Peer review confirms conclusions are supported with important controls. Peer R3 also includes integration efficiency claims (C93-C96, C102-C104) not in OpenEval R4.

Both evaluate promoter integration capability as SUPPORTED (C50-C51, C114-C119, C123-C124, C170). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative analysis of promoter recovery and size range compatibility. Peer review explicitly confirms the transcriptional reporter application is supported by data. Peer R4 includes additional landing pad design claims (C11, C105-C113, C120-C122, C125-C126) not in OpenEval R5.

Both evaluate landing pad designs as SUPPORTED (C52-C57). OpenEval R7 provides comprehensive molecular details including dual-selection requirement and homology arm specifications (C105-C112). Peer R5 highlights the clever design of selection markers as a strength. OpenEval covers more technical detail while peer review focuses on design innovation. Peer R5 also includes C58, C150-C151 not in OpenEval R7.

Both evaluate integration efficiency as SUPPORTED but with different claim coverage. OpenEval R6 focuses on efficiency metrics (C93-C96, C121, C129). Peer R7 covers error rates and practical recommendations (C127-C129, C132-C136), treating these as part of solid effectiveness data with important controls. Limited overlap (C129) but complementary aspects of integration performance.

Both address Sanger sequencing validation as SUPPORTED (C102-C104). OpenEval R8 focuses specifically on integration fidelity confirmation with appropriate caveats about small sample size. Peer R3 includes this validation data as part of broader integration efficiency and correlation findings (C49, C93-C101). Partial overlap with different emphasis.

Both evaluate error rates and quality control as SUPPORTED (C127-C128). OpenEval R9 provides detailed error rate analysis (~6-10%) and promoter recovery observations (C125-C126). Peer R7 treats error observations as part of overall effectiveness data. OpenEval provides more granular analysis while peer review accepts findings as practical considerations.

Both address co-conversion phenomenon as SUPPORTED (C132-C134). OpenEval R10 notes the ~50% co-conversion rate with caveat about limited shown data. Peer R7 includes co-conversion as part of broader integration efficiency findings. Both treat this as demonstrated but with limited examples.

Perfect claim overlap (C168-C169, C204-C205). Both evaluate expression pattern observations as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of microscopy data and nuclear localization patterns with appropriate acknowledgment of differences from prior reports. Peer review confirms expression characterization conclusions are supported by data as part of overall method validation.

Both address practical recommendations (C135-C136) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval R14 treats these as reasonable inferences from observed efficiency and error rates, representing appropriate user guidance. Peer R7 includes these recommendations as part of broader integration efficiency findings with solid effectiveness data.

Both evaluate the 1000-fold throughput increase claim as SUPPORTED (C187-C188). OpenEval R15 also addresses novelty claims (C171, C181) with comparison to prior methods showing orders of magnitude difference. Peer R9 confirms the throughput claim is central to the paper's significance and not questioned by reviewers. Both affirm this as a valuable contribution.

Both evaluate comparison to prior methods as SUPPORTED (C173-C180). OpenEval R16 provides detailed documentation of limitations in existing methods with appropriate citations. Peer R11 acknowledges the work adds to recent studies but provides practical protocol and tools, with advantages to emerge through general use. Both accept the comparison as valid context, though peer review notes methodological precedents.

Both address array formation mechanisms (C190-C196) as UNCERTAIN/SUPPORTED. OpenEval R17 rates as UNCERTAIN, noting mechanistic explanations are explicitly speculative despite well-supported observations. Peer R6 rates as SUPPORTED, treating these as important observations and considerations without challenging the speculative nature. Different evaluation types for similar speculative mechanistic content.

Perfect claim overlap (C197-C203). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative explanation about linear fragments (C202-C203) despite well-documented observations. Peer R12 rates as SUPPORTED, treating these as important observations and practical considerations for optimization. Different evaluation types: OpenEval emphasizes speculation, peer review accepts as practical findings.

Both evaluate adaptability to other systems (C13, C141, C146-C149, C152-C154) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval R19 notes these are speculative claims about future applications without experimental validation in other systems. Peer R10 explicitly states potential application beyond C. elegans remains speculative given the unique role of extrachromosomal arrays. Strong agreement on speculative nature.

Both address array overlap analysis and formation reproducibility as SUPPORTED (C80-C83 in OpenEval). OpenEval R12 provides detailed quantitative analysis of array independence and reproducibility. Peer R6 includes this as part of broader array formation observations. OpenEval focuses specifically on overlap metrics while peer review treats as part of general array characterization.

OpenEval R13 evaluates the rationale for using C. elegans and array biology properties (C42-C43, C143-C145) as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this background rationale, though peer R10 acknowledges the importance of extrachromosomal arrays as a unique feature.

OpenEval R20 evaluates background claims about transgenesis types and limitations (C1-C6, C14-C26) as SUPPORTED, providing appropriate context. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these background claims, as peer reviewers focus on primary results and method validation rather than contextual background.

OpenEval R21 evaluates survey of prior attempts (C27-C33) as SUPPORTED, documenting previous methods and their limitations. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this historical context, though peer R11 briefly mentions recent related studies when discussing methodological novelty.

Both address potential future applications as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval R22 covers broader speculative claims about barcoding applications (C137-C140, C155-C164) with citations to relevant methods. Peer R10 focuses specifically on cross-species adaptability (C155 overlap). Both recognize these as potential rather than demonstrated advantages, representing future directions.
